claim: R5-05 (b) set a budget: a change of the drawn week re-evaluates the chips within ≈ 100 ms of the frame being drawn, at the METROPOLIS cap. Rendering wrote it at §12.5 (base l. 17176–17179) and at T-ER-25's bar (l. 14753): "the chips re-evaluated within ≈ 100 ms of each scrubbed frame being drawn … the scrub clauses from the later of M5 and V06's E6". It also wrote it at §12.10's R12-35 (l. 17527). R12-35 names its measure as "V12 §3.15.10's `time.findSuggest` and `time.findGlow` (the glow from a chip's click, and from a scrubbed week's frame being drawn) … the scrubbed week's from the later of M5 and V06's E6", with the bar "≤ 100 ms (T120-6; T-ER-25)". The other two homes of the same timing still time only the click. The bar R12-35 cites, T120-6 (l. 18662–18663), reads "a chip's glow within ≈ 100 ms of its click (`time.findSuggest`, `time.findGlow` …)". §13.8's T120-6 row (l. 19373) reads "M5". V12's statistic follows the base bar: its catalogue row (V12 l. 1172) reads "a chip's click to its matches' glow drawn", and §3.15.10's T120-6 bullet (l. 2641–2643) says the same. T-V12-52 (l. 3174), which takes T120-6, plants no re-evaluation time and runs at M5 alone. VRC4T-04 asked that "R12-35's row and T120-6 add that timing", and R5-05's sweep lists "R12-35 and T120-6". Part H gives no END line for T120-6, which is scope's text. Rendering's two hand-offs, to scope and to V12, are open (repair-r5-rendering l. 133–141). V12 declined to write ahead of its home (repair-r5-V12, "Hand-offs received"). So the register's third bar reads a measurement that V12's statistic, as specified, never takes. A builder following V12 times only clicks. A builder following R12-35 also times the scrubbed frame. MAJOR: two builders build different behaviour, and the register needs an input that has no producer (VAP-r2-11's grade for a V12 statistic narrower than its base home).
required_change: §13.2's T120-6, after "a chip's glow within ≈ 100 ms of its click": add ", and at a drawn week whose frame is not the head the chips re-evaluated within ≈ 100 ms of that frame being drawn, the frame never waiting for them (§12.5; that clause from the later of M5 and V06's E6, V06 §3.15.2's frames)". §13.8's T120-6 row's milestone cell "M5" → "M5 (its drawn-week clause at the later of M5 and V06's E6)". V12's end, for an END line: - The catalogue row (l. 1172), "a chip's click to its matches' glow drawn" → "a chip's click to its matches' glow drawn, and a drawn week's frame (one that is not the head) drawn to its chips' re-evaluated glow drawn (from the later of M5 and V06's E6)". - §3.15.10's T120-6 bullet, "`time.findGlow` (a chip's click to its matches' glow drawn)" → "`time.findGlow` (a chip's click, and a scrubbed week's frame being drawn, to its matches' glow drawn — the latter from the later of M5 and V06's E6)". - T-V12-52, after "a planted suggestion time above §12.5's budget at the METROPOLIS cap fails its timing row": add "and a planted re-evaluation drawn more than 100 ms after a scrubbed week's frame fails `time.findGlow`'s". - T-V12-52's cell, "M5 (Find's milestone, §16)" → "M5 (Find's milestone, §16); its scrubbed-week glow at the later of M5 and V06's E6 (V06 §3.15.2's frames)".

claim: V12 and V08 register derived dossier fixtures in §13.2's fixture manifest: - V12 §1b (V12 l. 207–209): "the derived fixtures registered in §13.2's frozen fixture manifest (item 84; §17.1 (3) makes it the one door for a dossier into `plat/`)". The population row (l. 211) gives "a derived fixture `<dossier>@pop×k` in the manifest". - V12's spec field `dossier` (l. 633): "a fixture id of the frozen manifest …, a derived '<dossier>@pop×k' included". - V12 l. 1419: a population sweep or a landmark "enters as a fixture record of the frozen manifest". - V08 W93 (V08 l. 320) and V08 §7 (l. 3354): "their `@pop×k` derivatives registered in the frozen manifest". - V08 §7.1 (l. 3242): V12's item-122 and item-125 fixtures are "test-side mutations made here (X-V12-5), each in §13.2's frozen manifest". This round added three such mutations: the `metropolis-3` cap copy, `city-1`'s second fire and `town-1`'s severity-1 fire (V08's hand-off to scope). The home cannot hold them. §13.2's manifest (base l. 18307–18316) "holds one row per file". `DossierFixtureRow.kind` is `'birth'|'after-events'|'after-ticks'|'world-state'`, with no derived kind and no field naming a source file and its mutation. V08 §7.1 also says a mutation is "never written back into a fixture file". So a harness built to the base has no row for `town-1@pop×2` or the crisis copies, and one built to V12 looks them up there. The derived content is stated in each case, so nothing built or tested changes. This is a list that omits an id its readers name, graded minor.
